subject.title: refactor(prompt): use plain inbound context labels and drop system-tag sanitizer

question: Should OpenClaw standardize on the unforgeable inbound-context marker and trusted prompt narration as the replacement for rewriting system-looking text with `sanitizeInboundSystemTags` across gateway, hook, and queued-event paths?
rationale: This is a deliberate cross-cutting trust-boundary policy choice with compatibility and stored-state consequences; source-level review can assess implementation consistency but cannot choose the permanent security model.

options.title: Adopt the marker boundary
options.body: Approve the marker-plus-trusted-narration design, retaining the Doctor migrations and compatibility aliases, then require a rebase and final boundary proof.

options.title: Retain targeted sanitizer coverage
options.body: Keep sanitizer protection on externally sourced system-event paths while using plain labels and the marker for inbound context blocks.

options.title: Split the policy change
options.body: Land only the non-security label and SDK cleanup after separating the sanitizer-removal decision into a narrowly scoped review.

recommendation.title: Adopt the marker boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the marker-plus-trusted-narration design, retaining the Doctor migrations and compatibility aliases, then require a rebase and final boundary proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR history shows sustained ownership of the proposed marker, migration, and SDK compatibility implementation; final policy approval still requires a repository security owner.
